tickets.title: Best-Selling Category Products (DENSE_RANK)
tickets.description: Ranks products within each category by quantity sold and extracts the top 3 items.
tasks: Ranks products within each category by quantity sold and extracts the top 3 items.
learning_objectives: Understand relational database design and querying.
tickets.evaluation: `compare_result_set(actual, expected)` `check_command_used("DENSE_RANK()")` `check_command_used("OVER")` **[A] Correctness (40 pts)**: 40 pts for top 3 ranked items. **[B] Optimality (30 pts)**: 30 pts for utilizing CTE instead of subquery. **[C] Quality (20 pts)**: 20 pts for partitioning correctly.
common_mistakes: Forgetting semicolons at the end of statements.
Using reserved keywords as column names without backticks.
hints: Review the MySQL documentation for exact syntax.
Test your queries in smaller chunks first.

solution.query.sql:
WITH product_sales AS (
      SELECT
        p.category,
        p.name AS product_name,
        SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.category ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity) DESC) AS product_rank
      FROM order_items oi
      JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id
      GROUP BY p.category, p.name
    )
    SELECT category, product_name, total_units, product_rank
    FROM product_sales
    WHERE product_rank <= 3;

tickets.title: Month-over-Month Sales Growth (LAG)
tickets.description: Computes monthly revenue totals and MoM sales growth percentage compared to the previous month.
tasks: Computes monthly revenue totals and MoM sales growth percentage compared to the previous month.
learning_objectives: Understand relational database design and querying.
tickets.evaluation: `compare_result_set(actual, expected)` `check_command_used("LAG")` **[A] Correctness (40 pts)**: 40 pts for correct revenue growth math. **[B] Optimality (30 pts)**: 30 pts for clean CTE definitions. **[C] Quality (20 pts)**: 20 pts for handling division edge cases.
common_mistakes: Forgetting semicolons at the end of statements.
Using reserved keywords as column names without backticks.
hints: Review the MySQL documentation for exact syntax.
Test your queries in smaller chunks first.

solution.query.sql:
WITH monthly_rev AS (
      SELECT
        DATE_FORMAT(created_at, '%Y-%m') AS order_month,
        SUM(total_amount) AS revenue
      FROM orders
      WHERE status = 'completed'
      GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(created_at, '%Y-%m')
    )
    SELECT
      order_month,
      revenue,
      LAG(revenue, 1) OVER (ORDER BY order_month) AS prev_revenue,
      ROUND(
        ((revenue - LAG(revenue, 1) OVER (ORDER BY order_month)) / LAG(revenue, 1) OVER (ORDER BY order_month)) * 100,
        2
      ) AS growth_pct
    FROM monthly_rev;

tickets.title: Cumulative Customer Expenditure (SUM OVER)
tickets.description: Selects orders and calculates a running total of purchases for each customer over time.
tasks: Selects orders and calculates a running total of purchases for each customer over time.
learning_objectives: Understand relational database design and querying.
tickets.evaluation: `compare_result_set(actual, expected)` `check_command_used("SUM")` `check_command_used("PARTITION BY")` **[A] Correctness (40 pts)**: 40 pts for correct cumulative balances. **[B] Optimality (30 pts)**: 30 pts for using standard partitioning. **[C] Quality (20 pts)**: 20 pts for appropriate sorting on order timestamps.
common_mistakes: Forgetting semicolons at the end of statements.
Using reserved keywords as column names without backticks.
hints: Review the MySQL documentation for exact syntax.
Test your queries in smaller chunks first.

solution.query.sql:
SELECT
      id AS order_id,
      customer_id,
      total_amount,
      created_at,
      SUM(total_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY created_at) AS running_spent
    FROM orders
    WHERE status = 'completed';
